name: Standard pretraining
description: End-to-end backprop through a transformer, every weight updated every step.
notes: State at the scratch-trained rate b_w = 2.5 bits per weight (b_w.pretrained central) and a momentum-free optimizer, the attacker's choice; activations cross at 4 bits (b_a.activation central).

name: Standard pretraining, 8-bit boundaries
description: As backprop, with activations crossing at 8 bits as production systems send them.
notes: b_a.activation high.

name: Pretraining with a trained residual bottleneck
description: Backprop through an architecture whose residual crosses layer boundaries at half width.
notes: A linear d/2 bottleneck costs SWARM 26-28% more steps; not counted here (efficiency multiplier < 1).

name: Pretraining with a 1% residual subspace
description: Backprop through an architecture that confines the residual to 1% of its width at boundaries, 16 bits.
notes: The most aggressive published claim (Subspace Networks, unreplicated, mostly 2-8B).

name: DiLoCo (local SGD, sync every 30 steps)
description: Workers each run ordinary backprop on a full replica and average pseudo-gradients every H steps.
notes: Within a worker, blocks still pass the same state and activations as standard training, so its per-block traits equal backprop's: less traffic between workers does not shrink what crosses a block.

scaling.note: Derived: 0.66 at 35M, 0.95 at 2.4B; M = 1-2 about 1.0-1.1 at 2.4B.
Outperforms data-parallel with over 100x less communication.

name: Greedy layer-wise (local) learning
description: Each layer is trained with a local loss on the frozen prefix's outputs; no gradient crosses a layer boundary.
notes: No source in the index yet. Activations still cross forward; the thread theorem does not cover it, since it is not end-to-end backprop.

name: Full fine-tuning from a committed base
description: Backprop over every weight, starting from committed weights; the state is the delta.
notes: b_w.delta/sft central: 0.1 bits per base weight.

name: LoRA rank 16 on every matrix
description: Continued training of rank-16 adapters on every matrix, the base frozen.
notes: Updated fraction ~ 16 (1/7168 + 1/2048) for Kimi K2 shapes; bf16 adapter; 4 flops per active parameter per token (no weight gradients for the base); the adapter's up-projection has a 16-value entry fee.

name: RL with a rank-1 LoRA on every matrix
description: Rollouts and updates of rank-1 adapters on every matrix, including every routed expert.
notes: Priced at rollout cost (2 flops per active parameter per token, forward only); prompts are a small share of the tokens a rollout generates.

name: Expert-specialized fine-tuning (10% of experts)
description: Backprop that updates a tenth of the routed experts.
notes: b_w.delta/sft central.

name: Zeroth-order fine-tuning (MeZO, 20k steps)
description: Two forward passes per step with a seeded perturbation; the update is seeds and one scalar per step.
notes: The description does not split across slices: a block must read every seed to rebuild any slice. Decoding regenerates each step's perturbation, 10 flops per parameter per step.

name: Evolution strategies (population 30, 500 iterations)
description: Perturb, evaluate, and move along fitness-weighted seeded noise.
notes: 15,000 perturbations at 10 flops per parameter each.

name: Zeroth-order over a fixed 4096-seed pool
description: The update is one coefficient per seed of a fixed pool, so decoding costs the same for any run length.
notes: 4096 seeds at 10 flops per parameter each.

name: LSTM in place of the Transformer
description: Replace self-attention blocks with LSTM recurrence (the pre-2017 recipe).
notes: The one scale-dependent architecture multiplier; the reference already contains it. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Sequential recurrence: a block boundary in time carries the recurrent state; no attention.

scaling.metric: compute to loss threshold vs modern Transformer
scaling.note: 6.28x worse at loss 5.3, 26x worse at loss 4.4: the gap widens as loss falls.
LSTMs match on early tokens and fall behind on late ones.

multiplier.metric: compute to loss threshold vs modern Transformer

name: SwiGLU, rotary embeddings and pre-RMSNorm
description: Gated FFN (SwiGLU), rotary position encoding, and pre-normalization with RMSNorm.
notes: Each tweak is small and scale-invariant; they do not multiply (see the bundle). Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

name: Modern vs 2017 Transformer bundle
description: All post-2017 component changes together, at fixed scale.
notes: Stacked tweaks are sub-multiplicative; summing their log m_A overstates C_eff. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: Ablations multiply to 3.43x but the measured composite is 1.33x.

scaling.metric: combined CEG of compute-independent changes, nanoGPT

scaling.note: Most single modifications do not transfer.

name: Primer (squared ReLU + depthwise conv on Q, K, V)
description: Squared-ReLU FFN activation and a depthwise convolution after each attention projection.
notes: Baseline predates SwiGLU/RoPE; the gain over a modern baseline is unmeasured. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: Against a 2021 Transformer; 4x against original T5 at 500M.
Gains grow as a power law in compute.

name: Multi-query and sparse attention
description: Share K/V heads (MQA) or restrict attention to a sparse pattern, for cheaper inference.
notes: Training m_A below 1, approaching 1 with scale; a deployment choice, not a training gain. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Smaller KV state per token; no change to updated state.

scaling.metric: CEG vs standard attention, nanoGPT compact to full

multiplier.metric: CEG vs standard attention, nanoGPT compact to full

name: Kernel linear attention (Performer)
description: Replace softmax attention with a random-feature kernel approximation.
notes: m_A falls with scale. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: 2.7% vs 8.4% for the Transformer: a worse exponent.

name: Selective state-space models (Mamba, Mamba-2)
description: Replace attention with input-dependent linear recurrences (SSD).
notes: Loss m_A about 1 at small scale, below 1 on in-context abilities at 8B. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Per-token recurrent state of fixed size replaces the KV cache; boundary per token unchanged.

scaling.note: Mamba-3B matches Transformers twice its size (not compute-matched).
About 15 points behind the Transformer on in-context tasks.

name: Hybrid recurrence + attention (Griffin, Mamba-2-Hybrid)
description: Interleave linear-recurrent or SSM layers with a few (local or global) attention layers.
notes: m_A slightly above 1 and holding at 8B/3.5T; no equal-loss compute ratio published. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. 7% attention layers in the 8B hybrid; the rest carry a fixed-size recurrent state.

scaling.note: Lowest loss at every budget; slightly above 1.

scaling.metric: LM and retrieval benchmarks vs Mamba2

name: Linear RNNs (RWKV, HGRN2, TNL, xLSTM)
description: Linear-attention or gated linear recurrences with matrix or scalar memory.
notes: m_A about 1-1.2 on loss; below 1 on retrieval. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.metric: loss vs LLaMA at equal FLOPs, 70M-7B, 300B tokens
scaling.note: Same scaling trend, better perplexity, worse retrieval.

scaling.metric: quality at matched size, up to 14B

multiplier.metric: quality at matched size, up to 14B

name: Differential Transformer
description: Attention scores as the difference of two softmax maps, cancelling common-mode noise.
notes: Separate parameter and token savings of 1.5x; the compute-optimal m_A is likely about 1.5. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.metric: parameters or tokens to equal loss
scaling.note: About 65% of parameters or tokens, 830M-13B; 62.2% at 11B-equivalent.

multiplier.metric: parameters or tokens to equal loss

name: nGPT (normalized Transformer)
description: Normalize all embeddings, weights and hidden states to unit norm; layers move along the hypersphere.
notes: Step multipliers, unreplicated at scale; per-FLOP m_A unknown. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: 4-20x fewer steps depending on context length; per-step cost is higher.

name: Hyper-connections
description: Replace the residual stream by n parallel streams mixed by learned connection weights.
notes: Raises m_A while widening boundaries 4x, which raises the shard construction's cost. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. The hidden state is replicated n = 4 times, so each layer boundary carries 4x the values.

name: Byte Latent Transformer
description: Model raw bytes grouped into entropy-sized patches instead of a fixed tokenizer.
notes: m_A about 1; changes how novel data bits are counted. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Input is raw bytes at 8 bits each, so data bits per BPE-token-equivalent are higher.

scaling.metric: loss at equal training FLOPs vs Llama 3 BPE, up to 8B
scaling.note: Parity; up to 50% inference-FLOP savings at small loss cost.

multiplier.metric: loss at equal training FLOPs vs Llama 3 BPE, up to 8B

name: Looped / recursive Transformers (MoR, recurrent depth)
description: Reuse one block of layers several times per token, optionally with per-token recursion depth.
notes: m_A about 1 at small scale; concentrates many gates of work on few updated weights. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Unique updated weights per FLOP fall by the loop count (about 2x in MoR); same weights reused.

scaling.metric: validation loss at equal training FLOPs
scaling.note: Lower loss with nearly 50% fewer parameters at 16.5e18 FLOP.
Test-time depth up to 50B-equivalent compute at 3.5B unique parameters.

name: Fine-grained mixture of experts
description: Replace dense FFNs by many small routed experts (plus shared experts), activating a few per token.
notes: The largest and only clearly growing m_A, and it shrinks the state one token touches. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Active share 32B of 1.04T in Kimi K2 (the NCI board's row); E = 64 in Krajewski's fits gives an FFN active share of 1/64. Per-token updated state falls by the active share; routing adds all-to-all boundaries.

scaling.metric: compute to equal loss vs dense
scaling.note: 20x at 1e20, over 40x past 1e25 (extrapolated from 129M-3.7B fits, E = 64).

scaling.metric: literature estimate at fixed expert count
loss under a joint memory and compute budget
scaling.note: Still better than dense when total parameters are capped.

multiplier.metric: compute to equal loss vs dense

name: Coarse top-1/top-2 MoE (Switch, routed LMs)
description: Replace FFNs by FFN-sized experts with top-1 or top-2 routing.
notes: Coarse routing's m_A shrinks with N under fixed tokens; fine-grained MoE reverses this. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Active share about 1/E of FFN parameters for top-1 over E experts.

scaling.metric: step-time speedup to equal quality, T5-Base
scaling.note: Up to 7x; 4x over T5-XXL at trillion parameters.
Improvement shrinks with base size; zero past 937B (S-BASE) at 130B fixed tokens.

multiplier.metric: step-time speedup to equal quality, T5-Base

name: Unstructured / n:m weight sparsity
description: Train with a fixed fraction of weights pruned to zero.
notes: About 1 at Chinchilla allocation; a parameter-efficiency gain when over-training. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. At 75% sparsity a quarter of weight positions are updated and used.

scaling.note: Sparsity becomes optimal only when training well past Chinchilla.
Parameter multiplier in the infinite-data limit, not a compute multiplier.

name: Conditional depth (Mixture-of-Depths, progressive layer dropping)
description: Skip some layers for some tokens (MoD routing) or randomly and progressively during training (PLD).
notes: m_A about 1 against tuned baselines. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Per-token compute varies; layer boundaries are skipped by routed-out tokens.

scaling.note: Up to 1.5% better log-probability objective; m_A slightly above 1.

scaling.metric: pre-training time to equal downstream accuracy, BERT

scaling.note: Layer-dropping gains vanish against a tuned baseline.

multiplier.metric: pre-training time to equal downstream accuracy, BERT

name: Compute-optimal allocation (Chinchilla vs Kaplan)
description: Scale parameters and tokens equally (about 20 tokens per parameter) instead of N proportional to C^0.73.
notes: Part of the reference recipe; listed because it is the second scale-dependent gain. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.metric: CEG of Chinchilla over Kaplan allocation

scaling.note: 0.73 -> 0.5; the discrepancy came from last-layer cost, warmup and optimizer tuning.

multiplier.metric: CEG of Chinchilla over Kaplan allocation

name: Multi-epoch training on repeated data
description: Train for up to about 4 epochs over a smaller unique corpus.
notes: m_A about 1 while cutting novel data per token 4x. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Novel data bits per training token fall about 4x (17.3/4) if repeats are re-read from committed data.

scaling.metric: loss vs unique-data training, up to 9B / 900B tokens
scaling.note: Negligible loss change up to 4 epochs; value decays to zero beyond.

multiplier.metric: loss vs unique-data training, up to 9B / 900B tokens

name: Model-based quality filtering (FineWeb-Edu, DCLM)
description: Keep web documents a classifier rates as educational or high quality.
notes: Among the largest constant m_A; no change to NCI state. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: vs Llama 3 8B (other differences confound); 1.7x vs MAP-Neo.

name: Perplexity-based data pruning
description: Drop documents by a small reference model's perplexity.
notes: m_A about 1.45; the exponent change is unshown for LMs. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: Beats the baseline on as little as 30% of the data.
Exponential scaling in theory; metrics scale poorly to ImageNet.

name: Semantic deduplication and diversification (D4)
description: Cluster documents by embedding, remove near-duplicates and prototypical points.
notes: Small constant m_A. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

name: Domain reweighting and curricula (DoReMi, curriculum)
description: Choose domain mixture weights with a proxy model, or order data from easy to hard.
notes: m_A 1.2-2.6 against weak default mixtures. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: 18-45% fewer steps early; gains fade late in training.

name: Synthetic and rephrased pretraining data (WRAP, BeyondWeb, phi)
description: Train on web text rephrased or generated by an existing LLM, mixed with real data.
notes: Large m_A that excludes generation compute; the generator is a sunk model. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Generated text is still token ids (17.3 raw bits), but the generator's compute is a separate, uncounted circuit.

name: Multi-token prediction
description: Predict the next n tokens with n heads on a shared trunk.
notes: Task gains, not loss-based m_A. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.note: 12-17% more coding problems at 13B; increasingly useful with size.

name: UL2R mixture-of-denoisers continuation
description: Continue a causal LM briefly with UL2's mixture of denoising objectives.
notes: m_A about 2 on downstream metrics at frontier scale. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

scaling.metric: compute to equal downstream performance, PaLM 540B

multiplier.metric: compute to equal downstream performance, PaLM 540B

name: Masked diffusion language models
description: Train to denoise randomly masked tokens instead of left-to-right prediction.
notes: m_A 1/16 per FLOP with ample data; trades compute for data. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Up to 100 epochs nearly as good as fresh data: novel bits per training token about 17.3/100.

scaling.note: Overtakes AR past a critical compute when data is scarce.

name: SGD with momentum
description: Drop Adam's adaptive second moment.
notes: m_A about 0.53 for one fewer state word. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 64 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights + momentum.

scaling.note: The only optimizer clearly worse than Adam.

name: Muon (orthonormalized momentum)
description: Orthonormalize each matrix's momentum update by Newton-Schulz iteration.
notes: m_A about 1.1 near 1B and shrinking. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 64 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights + momentum; the orthonormalization reads whole matrices.

scaling.note: 1.4x at 0.1B to 1.1x at 1.2B; predicted below 1 at 7B, 1x Chinchilla.

name: Matrix and Hessian preconditioners (Shampoo, SOAP, Sophia)
description: Precondition with Kronecker-factored curvature (Shampoo, SOAP) or a diagonal Hessian estimate (Sophia).
notes: m_A 1.2-1.3 below 1B, shrinking with scale. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 2.5 bits per updated parameter. AdamW state plus Kronecker factors and eigenbases (SOAP); Sophia keeps two diagonal words like Adam.

scaling.metric: iterations to equal loss, large batch

scaling.note: Sophia's 2x claim falls to about 1 against tuned baselines: below AdamW at small compute, slightly above at larger size or data (Wen).

name: Lion and Adam-mini (one state word)
description: Sign-momentum update (Lion) or one second-moment value per parameter block (Adam-mini).
notes: m_A 0.95-1 for one fewer state word. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 64 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights + one moment.

scaling.note: At most 5% slower; Lion's gap widens and Adam-mini's narrows with scale.

name: Adafactor (factored second moment, no momentum)
description: Keep row and column sums of the second moment and drop momentum.
notes: m_A about 1 with a third of AdamW's per-parameter state. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 32 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights plus O(rows + columns) factors: about 32 bits per parameter.

name: 8-bit Adam (block-wise quantized state)
description: Store Adam's two moments in block-wise dynamic 8-bit quantization.
notes: m_A about 1. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 48 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights + two 8-bit moments.

name: SWAN (stateless normalized, whitened SGD)
description: Normalize and whiten each step's gradient; keep no optimizer state.
notes: m_A probably about 1 at Chinchilla budgets, with SGD's state. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 32 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights only.

scaling.note: Below 1x Chinchilla, where matrix optimizers gain most.

name: Learning-rate schedules (WSD, Schedule-Free)
description: Warmup-stable-decay or schedule-free averaging instead of cosine decay.
notes: m_A about 1. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

name: FP8 training
description: Run matmul inputs (and optionally optimizer moments) in E4M3/E5M2 with scaling.
notes: m_A about 1 per FLOP; per gate, an 8-bit multiplier is several times cheaper than bf16. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 48 bits per updated parameter. FP8 Adam moments as in Fishman 2024; master weights fp32.

scaling.note: 7-8 bits are compute-optimal, independent of compute.

name: FP4 training (NVFP4, Quartet)
description: Run matmul inputs in 4-bit block-scaled formats with Hadamard transforms and stochastic rounding.
notes: Per-FLOP m_A slightly below 1; per gate a large gain. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Master weights, gradients for accumulation and optimizer state stay fp32.

scaling.note: 1.5% relative loss gap; 0.5% after switching the forward pass to higher precision.
Competitive with FP8/FP16; loss gap tied to forward error.

name: Ternary-weight training (BitNet b1.58, Spectra)
description: Quantize forward weights to {-1, 0, 1} with high-precision latent weights.
notes: m_A about 1 at matched size above about 3B. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. 8-bit activations; latent weights and optimizer state stay high precision.

scaling.metric: perplexity at equal size and tokens

name: Streaming DiLoCo
description: Synchronize parameter fragments on a staggered schedule, overlapped with compute, in 4-bit.
notes: m_A about 1. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 2.5 bits per updated parameter. Each fragment syncs every H steps (H = 30-100 in its tables); FP4 communication.

scaling.note: Slightly better with 400x fewer bits exchanged.

name: DeMo (decoupled momentum)
description: Send only the top DCT components of the momentum each step; keep the rest local.
notes: m_A about 1. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 64 bits per updated parameter. fp32 weights + local momentum; per-step sync of a sparse update.

scaling.note: Up to 85x less data per GPU.

name: SparseLoCo (top-k, 2-bit pseudo-gradients)
description: DiLoCo with error feedback, top-k sparsification and 2-bit quantization of the outer update.
notes: m_A at or above DiLoCo's; updates are very low-entropy. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 2.5 bits per updated parameter. H = 15 in its tables; outer updates carry 1-3% of entries at 2 bits.

name: Subspace networks (compressed pipeline boundaries)
description: Confine activations and their gradients at pipeline cuts to a fixed low-dimensional subspace.
notes: m_A about 1 while cutting boundary width about 100x. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. About 100x fewer values per token cross each pipeline cut.

name: Branch-Train-Merge (embarrassingly parallel experts)
description: Train domain expert LMs independently from a shared seed model and ensemble or average them.
notes: Perplexity m_A about 2.5 for an ensemble; inference cost differs. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. No synchronization during expert training.

scaling.note: 22.4B total parameters vs a Transformer with 2.5x the compute; gains grow with domain count.

name: Greedy block-wise local learning
description: Split the network into K gradient-isolated blocks, each trained by its own auxiliary loss.
notes: m_A 0.6-0.85 by block count; halves boundary crossings. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Backprop stays inside each block; block boundaries carry forward activations only.

scaling.note: Derived from +0.062 nats; the K = 4 gap shrinks from 125M to 400M.

name: Forward gradients with local guesses
description: Estimate gradients by forward-mode directional derivatives along guessed directions.
notes: Per-FLOP m_A well below 1 and falling with dimension; no LM results. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Forward-mode JVPs only; usually paired with local losses.

scaling.note: Random guesses fail in high dimension; local-loss guesses help.

name: EGGROLL (low-rank evolution strategies)
description: Population-based ES with rank-r perturbations; update from fitness-weighted noise.
notes: Per-FLOP m_A far below 1; a data-efficiency, not compute-efficiency, method. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 8 bits per updated parameter. int8 weights; updates are seeds plus fitness scalars.

scaling.metric: GPU-hours vs backprop SGD, int8 RNN LM
scaling.note: Beats backprop at equal data with about 180x the GPU-hours.

name: Zeroth-order SGD (MeZO-style, DeepZero)
description: Estimate gradients from paired forward passes along random or coordinate perturbations.
notes: Per-FLOP m_A orders of magnitude below 1, shrinking with parameter count. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 16 bits per updated parameter. bf16 weights, no optimizer state; updates are seeds plus scalars.

scaling.metric: time to accuracy vs FO, Llama2-20M
scaling.note: Days vs hours; time is O(n) larger.
Approaches FO only on a small CNN.

name: Pre-training distillation
description: Train the student on a teacher's (truncated) next-token distribution alongside or instead of labels.
notes: Small m_A with a sunk teacher; about 70x more novel data bits per token. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Top-p-k teacher logits: about 15 TB over 100B tokens, about 1,200 bits per token.

scaling.metric: loss vs supervised at equal student compute
scaling.note: Better only below a crossover compute and only with a sunk teacher.

name: Structured pruning plus distillation (Minitron, Sheared LLaMA)
description: Prune a trained larger model and retrain it with distillation on a small token budget.
notes: Reuse of sunk compute, not an m_A for a fresh run. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Starts from committed teacher weights; per-step state as the reference.

scaling.metric: family compute vs training each from scratch

multiplier.metric: family compute vs training each from scratch

name: Depthwise stacking (G_stack)
description: Train a small model, stack its layers to initialize a deeper one, continue training.
notes: m_A about 1.5 at 7B. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. The growth step copies weights; training afterwards is standard.

name: Learned or function-preserving width growth (LiGO, HyperCloning)
description: Initialize a wider model from a smaller pretrained one by a learned or function-preserving map.
notes: m_A 2-4 excluding the small model's compute. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. As the reference except where stated.

name: Sparse upcycling (dense to MoE)
description: Initialize an MoE's experts from a dense checkpoint's FFNs and continue training.
notes: Reuse gain that shrinks with C. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. After upcycling, per-token state is the MoE's active share.

scaling.note: Beats dense with about 50% of the sunk cost.
An interaction term limits upcycling at large compute.

name: Retrieval-augmented pretraining (RETRO, kNN datastores)
description: Condition on chunks retrieved from a large datastore by a frozen retriever.
notes: Large parameter-equivalent gain; it raises novel data bits per token. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Retrieved neighbours are extra data read per token; the retriever is frozen.

scaling.note: Constant with model scale; a parameter (not compute) multiplier.

scaling.metric: loss at equal training compute vs datastore size
scaling.note: Improves without obvious saturation to 1.4T tokens.

name: Low-rank projected optimizer state (GaLore, APOLLO)
description: Keep Adam's moments in a rank-r projection of each gradient matrix (GaLore) or a random projection (APOLLO).
notes: m_A about 1 at 7B; state reduction, not update-rank reduction. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 48 bits per updated parameter. GaLore at r = 1024, d = 4096: 32 + 64 r/d = 48 bits; weights still all updated (full-rank over time).

scaling.note: Lags to 150B tokens, ahead from about 200B.

name: ReLoRA (merged low-rank updates)
description: Train low-rank adapters, merge them into the weights periodically, restart.
notes: m_A about 1 with a full-rank phase; low-rank updates between merges. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 2.5 bits per updated parameter. Between merges each update is rank r per matrix (r = 128 at 1.3B).

scaling.metric: perplexity vs full training, up to 1.3B
scaling.note: Needs a full-rank warm start (33% of steps at 1.3B).

multiplier.metric: perplexity vs full training, up to 1.3B

name: CoLA (low-rank bottleneck layers)
description: Replace full-size linear layers with auto-encoder pairs that enforce low-rank activations.
notes: Claimed m_A 2 on short budgets; unreplicated at Chinchilla allocation. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 96 bits per updated parameter. Default rank halves parameters and compute; internal bottlenecks narrow activations.

name: Dion (low-rank orthonormalized updates)
description: Amortized power iteration on momentum gives rank-r orthonormal updates with error feedback.
notes: Low-rank m_A approaches full-rank Muon with scale. Traits as published (from the scaling corpus): state at its stored precision, 64 bits per updated parameter. Each step's update and its communication are rank r (down to d/16).

scaling.note: Larger models increasingly robust to r = d/16.
